intro.title: A living archive of Africa.
intro.meaning: a broken piece of a pot, in [language]
paragraphs: African knowledge is like a broken pot: fragmented, scattered, with pieces of our stories, languages and traditions slowly being lost. Gae is our way of gathering those pieces back together, so they are never lost again.
We travel across Africa, starting in Kenya, to sit with elders, healers, rainmakers and artisans, to photograph communities and wildlife, and to keep records of artefacts and indigenous knowledge.

explore.text: Our first journey starts in Kajiado, near home, and then goes on to western Kenya, where our roots are.

myths.title: Myth, or meaning?
myths.text: African beliefs about animals, plants and places that were feared, dismissed or misunderstood. We go back to the communities who hold them and ask what they really mean.
myths.quote: “What the elders honoured, we were taught to fear.”

biodiversity.title: Biodiversity & Conservation
biodiversity.text: In Africa, people and the land cannot be separated. Clans have animal totems, trees are sacred, and healers know plants most of us have never heard of. When an animal or a forest disappears, a piece of our culture goes with it.
